function.mechanism: Technological polymer that provides binding, film-forming/coating, and stabilization effects; largely unabsorbed as part of the modified-cellulose group assessed by EFSA.

adi.basis: EFSA (2018 re-evaluation of celluloses including E462) concluded there is no need for a numerical ADI; consistent with JECFA/SCF ADI not specified approach.

efsa.key_finding: No safety concern at reported uses/use levels; no genotoxic concern and no carcinogenic signal in reviewed datasets for celluloses group including E462.

fda.cfr_citation: 21 CFR 172.868 (direct food additive); 21 CFR 182.90 (GRAS list for paper/paperboard migration)
fda.notes: Direct food uses are specified in 21 CFR 172.868; separate GRAS context exists for migration from paper/paperboard under 21 CFR 182.90.

adi.basis: WHO/JECFA database lists ETHYL CELLULOSE with ADI NOT SPECIFIED as part of group ADI for modified celluloses.

concerns.summary: Evidence base is stronger at grouped-cellulose level than highly additive-specific modern toxicology datasets for E462 alone.
Feed-additive EFSA opinions (2020, 2024) note insufficient data to conclude on user/handler safety, though consumer/environment conclusions were favorable.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA re-evaluation reported no genotoxic concern for celluloses including E462
EFSA re-evaluation reported no carcinogenic properties detected in the evaluated celluloses datasets
JECFA database lists ADI as not specified for modified celluloses including ethyl cellulose

adi_exceedance.notes: ADI is not specified (no numerical ADI), so classic ADI exceedance is not the primary risk metric; EFSA still concluded no safety concern at reported uses/use levels.

risk_assessment.rationale: Authoritative evaluations (EFSA/JECFA/FDA context) are consistently permissive for food uses at regulated conditions, with no strong genotoxic/carcinogenic signal. Remaining uncertainty is mainly the relative scarcity of modern E462-specific epidemiology/toxicology outside grouped-cellulose assessments.
key_factors: EFSA 2018 concluded no need for numerical ADI and no safety concern at reported uses
JECFA lists ADI as NOT SPECIFIED for modified celluloses including ethyl cellulose
US CFR explicitly permits direct uses in 21 CFR 172.868
No IARC classification entry identified for ethyl cellulose
Recent PubMed safety-oriented items are mostly regulatory updates rather than new harm signals
